Looking at the demo: the input is divided into blocks by full separator rows/columns (all one color, 0 in demo, 3 in test). Each block maps to one output cell. Demo blocks are 3x2 (5 row-groups × 4 col-groups → 5x4 output). Counting the minority color (8) per block: count 1 → output 5, count 2 → output 1. This matched all 20 demo cells perfectly.

Applying to the test (row groups of 4, two column groups; minority color 7): counts per block are 2,2 / 1,2 / 2,2 / 1,2 → output 1 1 / 5 1 / 1 1 / 5 1.

```python
def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    vals = set(v for row in grid for v in row)
    sep = None
    for v in vals:
        if any(all(c == v for c in row) for row in grid) and \
           any(all(grid[r][c] == v for r in range(h)) for c in range(w)):
            sep = v
            break
    # row groups: maximal runs of non-separator rows
    def groups(flags):
        gs, cur = [], []
        for i, f in enumerate(flags):
            if not f:
                cur.append(i)
            else:
                if cur: gs.append(cur); cur = []
        if cur: gs.append(cur)
        return gs
    rowg = groups([all(c == sep for c in row) for row in grid])
    colg = groups([all(grid[r][c] == sep for r in range(h)) for c in range(w)])
    cnt = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != sep)
    minority = min(cnt, key=lambda k: cnt[k])
    out = []
    for rg in rowg:
        row = []
        for cg in colg:
            n = sum(1 for r in rg for c in cg if grid[r][c] == minority)
            row.append(5 if n == 1 else 1)
        out.append(row)
    return out
```

def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    vals = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    sep = None
    for v in vals:
        if any(all(c == v for c in row) for row in grid) and \
           any(all(grid[r][c] == v for r in range(h)) for c in range(w)):
            sep = v
            break
    def groups(flags):
        gs, cur = [], []
        for i, f in enumerate(flags):
            if not f: cur.append(i)
            else:
                if cur: gs.append(cur); cur = []
        if cur: gs.append(cur)
        return gs
    rowg = groups([all(c == sep for c in row) for row in grid])
    colg = groups([all(grid[r][c] == sep for r in range(h)) for c in range(w)])
    cnt = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != sep)
    majority = max(cnt, key=lambda k: cnt[k])
    out = []
    for rg in rowg:
        row = []
        for cg in colg:
            n = sum(1 for r in rg for c in cg if grid[r][c] != sep and grid[r][c] != majority)
            row.append(majority if n == 1 else 1)
        out.append(row)
    return out
